title: Breaking the Reference Bottleneck via Learning to Rewrite Conversational Queries without Gold Reference Passages
claim: One model can serve two roles at once, rewriting the query and refining the response, because both rely on shared context.
layout: Single panel, inputs left to center module to outputs right, thought-bubble clouds
description: A hub-and-spoke diagram with a yellow box labeled CQR at the center. On the left, three rounded boxes feed into it with curved arrows: Conversation (grey, with the turn 'Who wrote Moby-Dick' and the answer 'Melville'), Query (green, 'what is it about?') and Response (blue, 'A story of a whale'). Two cloud thought-bubbles attach to the CQR box. The top cloud, 'Query's Context', says 'it' = 'Moby-Dick'. The bottom cloud, 'Response's Context', says 'story' = 'Moby-Dick'. On the right, two arrows lead out. A green Reformulated Query box reads 'what is Moby-Dick by Melville about?'. A blue Refined Response box reads 'Moby-Dick by Melville: A story of a whale'. Colors pair each input with its output. The eye goes first to the central CQR box.
caption: Overview of \algname{}. (a) Preference optimization framework for CQR with reference passages as a key component for generating preference feedback over candidate queries. (b) Key idea of \algname{}: Inferring pseudo reference passages through response refinement, addressing ambiguities and omissions in raw responses by incorporating conversational context.
abstract: Conversational query reformulation (CQR) has become indispensable for improving retrieval in dialogue-based applications. However, existing approaches typically rely on reference passages for optimization, which are impractical to acquire in real-world scenarios. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel reference-free preference optimization framework DualReform that generates pseudo reference passages from commonly-encountered conversational datasets containing only queries and responses. DualReform attains this goal through two key innovations: (1) response-based inference , where responses serve as proxies to infer pseudo reference passages, and (2) response refinement via the dual-role of CQR , where a CQR model refines responses based on the shared objectives between response refinement and CQR. Despite not relying on reference passages, DualReform achieves 96.9--99.1% of the retrieval accuracy attainable only with reference passages and surpasses the state-of-the-art method by up to 31.6%.
